meta.title: Nephrology Literature Update
meta.query: Clinical nephrology — RCTs, systematic reviews & meta-analyses (humans, English)
meta.source: PubMed (NLM) abstracts; summaries and appraisals generated automatically from those abstracts. Each entry links to its PubMed record and DOI.
meta.note: Summaries and PICO are machine analyses of the source abstracts; criteria marked “not specified” were not stated. Read the source before acting clinically.
meta.appraisal_source: Automated critical appraisal (clinical bottom-line, relevance, caveat).

articles.authors: Pei X, Gao H, Zhang L
articles.title: Diagnostic and prognostic value of fibroblast growth factor 23 in acute kidney injury: systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 23 studies (17 diagnostic, 6 prognostic) evaluating circulating iFGF23 or cFGF23 in AKI. For AKI diagnosis, the pooled sensitivity was 0.79 (95% CI 0.73-0.86), specificity was 0.82 (95% CI 0.75-0.89), PLR was 4.40 (95% CI 2.59-6.21), NLR was 0.25 (95% CI 0.16-0.34), DOR was 17.49 (95% CI 8.67-35.16), and SROC AUC was 0.87 (95% CI 0.81-0.92). For AKI mortality, pooled sensitivity was 0.77 (95% CI 0.69-0.84), specificity was 0.76 (95% CI 0.70-0.82), DOR was 10.89 (95% CI 6.86-17.30), and SROC AUC was 0.77 (95% CI 0.70-0.83).

pico.population: Patients at risk of or with acute kidney injury (AKI)
pico.intervention: Measurement of circulating intact FGF23 (iFGF23) or C-terminal FGF23 (cFGF23)
pico.comparison: Standard diagnostic/prognostic methods or no FGF23 measurement
pico.outcome: AKI diagnosis (sensitivity, specificity, SROC AUC) and AKI mortality

inclusion: Studies evaluating circulating intact FGF23 (iFGF23) or C-terminal FGF23 (cFGF23) for AKI diagnosis or prognosis

appraisal.bottom_line: Circulating FGF23 exhibits moderate-to-high diagnostic performance (SROC AUC 0.87) and moderate prognostic performance for mortality (SROC AUC 0.77) in patients with AKI, with iFGF23 showing higher diagnostic accuracy than cFGF23.
appraisal.relevance: FGF23 could serve as a valuable complementary biomarker for early AKI detection and risk stratification in clinical settings.
appraisal.caveat: The analysis is limited by substantial heterogeneity among the included studies (I2 = 67% for diagnosis, and up to 86.2% for mortality sensitivity) and a lack of standardized measurement protocols.

articles.authors: Thomas SM, Anilkumar AS, Veerabathiran R
articles.title: Protective association of the ELMO1 rs741301 variant against diabetes mellitus and diabetic nephropathy: a systematic meta-analysis of case-control studies.
articles.summary: A systematic meta-analysis of 9 case-control studies (880 individuals with DM and 1008 with DN) evaluating the association between the ELMO1 rs741301 polymorphism and DN. The pooled analysis demonstrated a significant protective association under the allelic model (OR = 0.77, 95% CI: 0.67-0.88), recessive model (OR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.61-0.90), and dominant model (OR = 0.68, 95% CI: 0.53-0.88).

pico.population: Individuals with diabetes mellitus (DM) and diabetic nephropathy (DN)

inclusion: Case-control studies investigating the association between ELMO1 rs741301 and DN among individuals with DM published between 2014 and 2024

appraisal.bottom_line: The ELMO1 rs741301 polymorphism is significantly associated with reduced susceptibility to diabetic nephropathy among individuals with diabetes under allelic, recessive, and dominant genetic models.
appraisal.relevance: Identifying genetic protective factors like ELMO1 rs741301 may help risk-stratify diabetic patients and improve our understanding of the genetic architecture of diabetic kidney disease.
appraisal.caveat: This meta-analysis is based entirely on observational case-control studies, which cannot establish causality, and the total sample size across the 9 included studies is relatively small.

articles.authors: Ma J, Liu B, Pang J, Wang P, Li Y et al.
articles.title: Efficacy and safety of ferric citrate tablets in Chinese patients with hyperphosphatemia undergoing maintenance hemodialysis: a multicenter, randomized, open-label, active-controlled, phase III trial.
articles.summary: A multicenter, randomized, open-label, phase III trial of 239 Chinese patients with hyperphosphatemia on maintenance hemodialysis randomized to ferric citrate (n=119) or sevelamer carbonate (n=120) for 12 weeks. The mean change in serum phosphorus was -0.70 +/- 0.50 mmol/L in the ferric citrate group and -0.61 +/- 0.59 mmol/L in the sevelamer group (least squares mean difference, -0.09 mmol/L; 95% CI, -0.24 to 0.05 mmol/L), demonstrating non-inferiority within the 0.32 mmol/L margin.

pico.population: Chinese patients with hyperphosphatemia undergoing maintenance hemodialysis (MHD)
pico.outcome: Change in serum phosphorus levels from baseline to week 12

inclusion: Patients with hyperphosphatemia on maintenance hemodialysis

appraisal.bottom_line: Ferric citrate tablets are non-inferior to sevelamer carbonate in lowering serum phosphorus levels in Chinese hemodialysis patients over 12 weeks, while also improving iron-related parameters and hemoglobin.
appraisal.relevance: Ferric citrate provides a useful dual-action therapeutic option to manage both hyperphosphatemia and renal anemia simultaneously, potentially reducing pill burden.
appraisal.caveat: The trial was open-label and limited to a relatively short duration of 12 weeks, which may not capture long-term safety, adherence, or potential iron overload issues.

articles.authors: Yan Z, Yu C, Zhang J, Wu M, Liu X et al.
articles.title: Outcomes and learning curve of single-kidney transplantation from small pediatric donors in children: a retrospective cohort study with meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A retrospective cohort study of 77 children (26 small-donor vs 51 large-donor) and meta-analysis of 7 studies (527 patients). In the cohort, the small-donor group had lower 1-year graft survival (73.1% vs 100%, P < 0.001) and higher acute rejection (19.2% vs 2.0%, P = 0.026). Meta-analysis showed 1-year patient survival of 98%, graft survival of 91%, and pooled thrombosis, DGF, and acute rejection rates of 5%, 13%, and 10%, respectively.

pico.intervention: Single-kidney transplantation from small pediatric donors (weight ≤ 15 kg or age ≤ 3 years)
pico.comparison: Single-kidney transplantation from large pediatric donors
pico.outcome: 1-year graft and patient survival, acute rejection, thrombosis, delayed graft function (DGF), eGFR, and operative learning curve

inclusion: Pediatric patients undergoing single-kidney transplantation from small pediatric donors (weight ≤ 15 kg or age ≤ 3 years) or large pediatric donors

appraisal.bottom_line: Single-kidney transplantation from small pediatric donors is associated with lower 1-year graft survival (73.1% vs 100%) and higher acute rejection (19.2% vs 2.0%) compared to larger donors, though outcomes improve after a learning curve of approximately 15 cases.
appraisal.relevance: Utilizing small pediatric donors can expand the donor pool for children, but centers must be prepared for higher early graft loss and a distinct technical learning curve.
appraisal.caveat: The cohort study was retrospective, single-center, and small (n=77), and the meta-analysis is limited by the observational nature of the included studies.

articles.authors: Mojtahedi SY, Sedighiyan M, Pourpashang P
articles.title: Association between vitamin D deficiency and chronic kidney disease progression: A GRADE-based dose-response systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of 11 observational/cohort studies. Vitamin D deficiency was associated with 33% higher odds of CKD progression (OR = 1.33, 95% CI: 1.06-1.67; P = 0.019; I2 = 98.2%). Dose-response analysis of 10 studies suggested higher odds of CKD progression per 10 ng/mL lower 25(OH)D concentration (OR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.09-1.25).

pico.intervention: Low serum vitamin D levels (deficiency or lower 25(OH)D concentration)
pico.comparison: Normal or higher serum vitamin D levels

inclusion: Observational and cohort studies published between 1990 and 2024 reporting baseline vitamin D levels and CKD progression outcomes

appraisal.bottom_line: Lower serum 25(OH)D levels are associated with increased odds of CKD progression (OR 1.33 for deficiency; OR 1.18 per 10 ng/mL lower level), but the certainty of evidence is very low.
appraisal.relevance: While vitamin D deficiency correlates with worse renal outcomes, this observational data does not prove that vitamin D supplementation prevents CKD progression.
appraisal.caveat: The analysis is based entirely on observational studies with massive heterogeneity (I2 = 98.2%), and the dose-response analysis relied on reconstructed category-level exposure values.

articles.authors: Saleh SE, Elnagar SSE, Fouda MA, Sayed-Ahmed N
articles.title: Effects of probiotic supplementation on disease progression in patients with moderate to severe chronic kidney disease: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.summary: A double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of 72 patients with CKD stages 3 or 4 receiving Lactobacillus plantarum (10^10 CFU daily) or placebo for six months. The probiotic group demonstrated a significant increase in eGFR compared to a significant decline in the placebo group. No probiotic participants experienced CKD progression compared to 8.6% in the placebo group.

pico.intervention: Lactobacillus plantarum (10^10 CFU daily) for six months
pico.outcome: Change in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), urinary indoxyl sulfate levels, and CKD progression rate

appraisal.bottom_line: Supplementation with Lactobacillus plantarum for 6 months significantly improved eGFR and prevented CKD progression compared to placebo, independent of changes in urinary indoxyl sulfate.
appraisal.relevance: Targeting the gut-kidney axis with specific probiotics may represent a novel, low-risk therapeutic strategy to slow CKD progression.
appraisal.caveat: The study had a very small sample size (n=72) and a short follow-up duration (6 months), and the exact mechanism of eGFR improvement remains unclear since indoxyl sulfate levels did not change.

articles.authors: Zhang Q, Gong T, Ye Y
articles.title: The Impact of Educational or Behavioural Interventions on Fatigue in Adults Receiving Haemodialysis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 30 studies evaluating non-pharmacological interventions for fatigue in adults receiving hemodialysis. Self-management education significantly reduced fatigue (SMD = 0.98, 95% CI [0.69, 1.28], p < 0.001), as did exercise training (SMD = 0.82, 95% CI [0.44, 1.20], p < 0.001). Cognitive behavioral therapy did not show a significant effect (SMD = 1.45, 95% CI [-0.46, 3.37], p = 0.137).

pico.intervention: Self-management education, exercise training, or cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT)
pico.outcome: Fatigue (standardised mean differences based on change scores)

inclusion: Randomised controlled trials and quasi-experimental studies evaluating educational or behavioural interventions on fatigue in adults receiving haemodialysis, searched from database inception to January 27, 2026

appraisal.bottom_line: Self-management education (SMD 0.98) and exercise training (SMD 0.82) significantly reduce fatigue in hemodialysis patients, whereas cognitive behavioral therapy does not show a statistically significant effect.
appraisal.relevance: Incorporating structured self-management education and exercise programs into dialysis care plans can help address the highly prevalent and debilitating symptom of fatigue.
appraisal.caveat: The meta-analysis included quasi-experimental studies alongside RCTs, and the certainty of evidence was low for exercise and very low for CBT, indicating potential bias and heterogeneity.

articles.authors: Jothi P, Murugesan RP, Dhakshinamoorthy J, M AK
articles.title: Renal Rehabilitation and Its Relationship with Anemia, Nutritional Status, and Activities of Daily Living in Patients Undergoing Maintenance Hemodialysis: A Systematic Review.
articles.summary: A qualitative systematic review of 42 studies published between 2015 and 2025 evaluating the effects of renal rehabilitation (structured exercise, nutritional support, and multidisciplinary interventions) on adults undergoing maintenance hemodialysis. Renal rehabilitation was associated with modest improvements in hemoglobin levels, ESA responsiveness, and nutritional parameters, with consistent benefits in functional outcomes (exercise capacity, muscle strength, frailty, and activities of daily living).

pico.intervention: Renal rehabilitation (structured exercise, nutritional support, and multidisciplinary interventions)
pico.outcome: Anemia (hemoglobin, ESA responsiveness), nutritional status, and activities of daily living (exercise capacity, muscle strength, frailty)

inclusion: Studies published between 2015 and 2025 evaluating the effects of renal rehabilitation on anemia, nutritional status, and activities of daily living in adults undergoing maintenance hemodialysis

appraisal.bottom_line: Renal rehabilitation is associated with modest improvements in hemoglobin and nutritional parameters, with its most consistent benefits seen in functional outcomes like exercise capacity, muscle strength, and activities of daily living.
appraisal.relevance: Implementing structured exercise and multidisciplinary rehabilitation can help combat frailty and improve the functional independence of maintenance hemodialysis patients.
appraisal.caveat: This is a qualitative systematic review of highly heterogeneous interventions and study designs, lacking a quantitative meta-analysis to provide pooled effect sizes.

articles.authors: Wang D, Wang Z, Wang D, Lei W, Lu Y et al.
articles.title: Effects of flurbiprofen axetil on postoperative renal function in patients undergoing percutaneous nephrolithotomy: A prospective, randomized, double-blind, controlled clinical study.
articles.summary: A prospective, randomized, double-blind, controlled study of 120 patients undergoing PCNL randomized to postoperative flurbiprofen axetil (100 mg IV, n=60) or saline (n=60). AKI occurred in 5 cases in the control group vs 1 case in the flurbiprofen group (P = 0.207). At 6 hours postoperatively, NGAL levels were significantly lower in the flurbiprofen group (184.84 +/- 43.14 vs 216.35 +/- 63.39, P = 0.002).

pico.population: Patients undergoing percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) under general anesthesia
pico.outcome: Incidence of perioperative acute kidney injury (AKI), and postoperative levels of serum creatinine, GFR, cystatin C, and NGAL

inclusion: Patients undergoing PCNL under general anesthesia between February and July 2025

appraisal.bottom_line: Postoperative administration of 100 mg flurbiprofen axetil did not significantly reduce the incidence of clinical AKI (1 case vs 5 cases, P=0.207), though it was associated with lower NGAL levels at 6 hours postoperatively.
appraisal.relevance: NSAIDs like flurbiprofen axetil are often avoided postoperatively due to nephrotoxicity concerns; this study suggests low-dose use might not worsen, and could potentially mitigate, early subclinical tubular injury markers.
appraisal.caveat: The study was underpowered to detect a difference in clinical AKI (only 6 total cases occurred), and the primary positive finding was a transient difference in a surrogate biomarker (NGAL at 6 hours) with no differences in creatinine or cystatin C at other time points.

articles.authors: Aziz A, Abbas S, Aftab A, Naqvi R
articles.title: Poisons causing acute kidney injury in Indo-Pak region: A meta-analysis.
articles.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 19 studies (12 from India, 7 from Pakistan; total population 3,769) on poisoning-induced AKI. Ten studies focused on paraphenylene diamine (PPD) poisoning. The pooled mortality was 20-23%, with fixed-effect and random-effect model estimates of 0.23 (95% CI: 0.22-0.25) and 0.20 (95% CI: 0.12-0.28), respectively, with high heterogeneity (I2 = 90%).

pico.population: Patients with acute kidney injury due to poisoning in India and Pakistan
pico.intervention: Exposure to various poisons (e.g., paraphenylene diamine, paraquat, organophosphate, copper sulphate, methyl alcohol, rodenticides)
pico.comparison: Not applicable (epidemiological meta-analysis of exposure outcomes)
pico.outcome: All-group mortality and sub-group mortality for paraphenylene diamine poisoning

inclusion: Studies from India and Pakistan reporting on acute kidney injury resulting from exposure to different poisons

appraisal.bottom_line: Poisoning-induced AKI in the Indo-Pak region is associated with a high pooled mortality rate of 20% to 23%, with paraphenylene diamine (PPD) being the most frequently studied offending agent.
appraisal.relevance: Understanding the local epidemiology of nephrotoxic poisons is critical for clinicians in South Asia to ensure rapid recognition and targeted management.
appraisal.caveat: The meta-analysis is limited by extreme heterogeneity (I2 = 90%) and significant publication bias among the included observational studies, which varied widely in the types of poisons and clinical settings.

articles.authors: Pourrezagholi F, Amini H, Omid Moradi, Mahdavi B, Nadiri Niri A et al.
articles.title: Effect of Melatonin Supplementation on Glycemic and Lipid Profiles in Kidney Transplant Recipients: A Clinical Trial.
articles.summary: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 84 kidney transplant recipients randomized to 6 mg/day melatonin (n=42) or placebo (n=42) for three months. Melatonin significantly decreased FBS (median -6.5 mg/dL, P < 0.001) and HbA1c (-0.25 units, P < 0.001) from baseline. The adjusted between-group effect favored melatonin for HbA1c (beta = -0.30%; 95% CI: -0.59 to -0.01; P < 0.001) and triglycerides (adjusted beta = -23.77 mg/dL; 95% CI: -45.50 to -2.04; P = 0.032), but not for FBS (beta = -2.61 mg/dL; 95% CI: -17.93 to 12.71; P = 0.283).

pico.population: Adult kidney transplant recipients (≥6 months post-transplant)
pico.intervention: Melatonin supplementation (6 mg/day) for three months
pico.outcome: Changes in fasting blood sugar (FBS), HbA1c, blood pressure, and lipid profile parameters (triglycerides)

inclusion: Adult kidney transplant recipients (≥6 months post-transplant)

appraisal.bottom_line: Melatonin supplementation (6 mg/day) for 3 months modestly improved glycemic control (HbA1c beta = -0.30%) and lowered triglycerides (beta = -23.77 mg/dL) in kidney transplant recipients, without affecting blood pressure or kidney function.
appraisal.relevance: Melatonin may serve as a safe, low-cost adjuvant therapy to manage post-transplant metabolic complications like dyslipidemia and hyperglycemia.
appraisal.caveat: The study had a small sample size (n=84) and a short duration (3 months), and the primary glycemic endpoint of fasting blood sugar did not show a statistically significant difference between groups in the adjusted analysis.

articles.authors: Shadravan S, Khezri R, Zarei Venovel M, Mahami-Oskouei M, Hooman N
articles.title: Impact of Dapagliflozin on Kidney Function Decline in Chronic Kidney Disease Patients: A Systematic Review.
articles.summary: A systematic review of 15 publications evaluating dapagliflozin in CKD. After excluding 11 overlapping publications from the DAPA-CKD trial, 4 unique independent trials were analyzed. The mean difference in eGFR decline ranged from -6.60 mL/min/1.73m² to +0.93 mL/min/1.73m². Substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 93.7%) precluded meta-analysis.

pico.outcome: Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline and composite renal outcomes

inclusion: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) concerning dapagliflozin in individuals with CKD, searched up to January 10, 2025
exclusion: Publications with overlapping populations (e.g., secondary analyses of the DAPA-CKD parent trial)

appraisal.bottom_line: The impact of dapagliflozin on eGFR decline was highly variable across four unique trials (ranging from -6.60 to +0.93 mL/min/1.73m²), and extreme heterogeneity (I2 = 93.7%) prevented a quantitative meta-analysis.
appraisal.relevance: While the landmark DAPA-CKD trial established clear clinical benefits, this review highlights that smaller, independent trials show highly variable short-term eGFR changes.
appraisal.caveat: The systematic review was severely limited by the lack of independent large-scale RCTs, as 11 of the 15 identified papers were redundant publications from the single DAPA-CKD trial.

articles.authors: Liu PY, Shih CK, Hsieh MH, Lin CC, Liu CY et al.
articles.title: Cardiovascular outcome of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists vs dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor on end-stage kidney disease patients with heart failure: an emulated target trial in patients with diabetes.
articles.summary: An emulated target trial using the TriNetX network comparing GLP-1RAs vs DPP-4is in diabetic ESKD patients with HF on maintenance dialysis. GLP-1RA use was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite ischemic cardiovascular events plus HF exacerbations (31.7% vs 41.4%; HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.64-0.82, P < 0.0001), lower ischemic events (HR 0.74), lower HF exacerbations (HR 0.76), and lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.68).

pico.population: Diabetic end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) patients with heart failure (HF) undergoing maintenance dialysis
pico.intervention: Initiation of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs)
pico.outcome: Primary composite of ischemic cardiovascular events plus HF exacerbations, individual components, and all-cause mortality

inclusion: Diabetic ESKD patients with HF undergoing maintenance dialysis (identified via TriNetX federated electronic health record network)

appraisal.bottom_line: In diabetic ESKD patients with heart failure on dialysis, initiation of GLP-1RAs was associated with a 28% lower risk of composite cardiovascular events/HF exacerbations (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.64-0.82) and a 32% lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR 0.68) compared to DPP-4is.
appraisal.relevance: This study provides much-needed real-world evidence for a high-risk population (dialysis patients with HF) that is typically excluded from large cardiovascular outcome trials of GLP-1RAs.
appraisal.caveat: Although labeled as a 'Randomized controlled trial' in PubMed publication types, this is actually an observational target trial emulation using electronic health records, which is subject to residual confounding despite propensity score matching.
